PERF-PY-1.name: Full Result Set Materialized Before App-Side Sort
PERF-PY-1.original_description: Detect ORM scalar materialization followed by sorted() for aggregate-style reads.
PERF-PY-1.description: A SQLAlchemy result is fully materialized into Python and then sorted to calculate an aggregate or percentile. The transfer and O(N log N) sort grow with the queried window; prefer a database aggregate, ordered aggregate, or maintained rollup when database semantics support it.
PERF-PY-1.detection_notes: Match result.scalars().all() or execute(...).all() assigned to a name that reaches sorted(...), list.sort(), or percentile-like index arithmetic in the same function. Do not flag bounded administrative exports or code already using SQL aggregate/window functions.

PERF-PY-2.name: Django ORM Lookup Inside Item Loop
PERF-PY-2.original_description: Detect Django QuerySet get/filter operations repeated for each collection item.
PERF-PY-2.description: A Django ORM lookup executes inside a loop over request or batch items. This produces one or more database round trips per item; collect keys and fetch the required rows in one query before the loop when the operation does not require distinct locking decisions.
PERF-PY-2.detection_notes: Match Model.objects.get, filter, first, or select_for_update().first inside a for-loop body. Report only when the lookup uses a loop-derived value or repeats a loop-invariant lookup. Suppress loops over a small explicit tuple/list of at most two items and deliberately paged management commands.

PERF-PY-3.name: Django Per-Row Create In Batch Loop
PERF-PY-3.original_description: Detect repeated Django ORM create calls in a batch loop.
PERF-PY-3.description: A Django model is created once per loop iteration for a batch of independent rows. Per-row INSERTs multiply network and transaction overhead; build model instances and use bulk_create when model hooks, generated keys, and conflict semantics permit it.
PERF-PY-3.detection_notes: Match Model.objects.create(...) inside a for-loop. Suppress when the created row is immediately required for a dependent query, when create has an explicit comment documenting signal/side-effect requirements, or when the batch is statically tiny.

PERF-PY-4.name: Django Read-Modify-Write Counter Update
PERF-PY-4.original_description: Detect model field arithmetic followed by save instead of an atomic update.
PERF-PY-4.description: A Django model field is read into Python, incremented or decremented, and saved. On a hot path this adds a read-modify-write round trip and can lose concurrent updates; prefer QuerySet.update with F() expressions when the update does not need model save hooks.
PERF-PY-4.detection_notes: Match obj.field += value or obj.field -= value followed by obj.save() in the same function or loop. Require a numeric-looking field name such as quantity, stock, count, balance, available, or reserved. Do not report explicit F() updates or functions whose save hook is documented as required.

PERF-PY-5.name: Sequential Blocking Delivery Over Claimed Batch
PERF-PY-5.original_description: Detect synchronous network delivery serially iterated over a claimed work batch.
PERF-PY-5.description: A worker claims a batch and invokes blocking network delivery once per item in a serial loop. Queue latency becomes the sum of each partner timeout; use bounded concurrency with per-endpoint limits after the claim operation is made atomic.
PERF-PY-5.detection_notes: Match a function named run_once, worker, deliver, dispatch, or process that obtains a batch/list and then calls requests.*, session.request, client.send, deliver, or dispatch inside a for-loop. Suppress when a bounded executor, semaphore, pool.map, gather with a limit, or explicit per-endpoint limiter is in the enclosing function.

PERF-PY-6.name: ORM Work Claim Without Row Lock
PERF-PY-6.original_description: Detect status claims that select work and update it without a locking or atomic claim operation.
PERF-PY-6.description: A queue worker selects pending ORM rows and changes their status in a later statement without a row lock or atomic update. Concurrent workers can claim and deliver the same work, increasing load as well as violating delivery ownership; use a transaction with skip-locked row selection or an equivalent atomic claim.
PERF-PY-6.detection_notes: Match QuerySet/query.filter(...pending...) followed by .all()/first() and later item.status assignment plus commit/save in the same function. Suppress when the query uses select_for_update, with_for_update, skip_locked, an UPDATE ... RETURNING claim, or a documented single-process worker.

PERF-PY-7.name: BaseHTTPMiddleware On FastAPI Request Path
PERF-PY-7.original_description: Detect Starlette BaseHTTPMiddleware subclasses registered on a FastAPI app.
PERF-PY-7.description: FastAPI or Starlette registers a BaseHTTPMiddleware subclass on the request path. Its task and streaming behavior can add avoidable overhead; prefer a pure ASGI middleware for simple header, timing, or request-state work after preserving response semantics.
PERF-PY-7.detection_notes: Match class X(BaseHTTPMiddleware) together with app.add_middleware(X), decorator-based registration, or a middleware list containing X. Do not flag third-party middleware whose implementation cannot be replaced safely; report project-defined subclasses only.

PERF-PY-8.name: SQLAlchemy Lazy Relationship Access In Batch Loop
PERF-PY-8.original_description: Detect ORM relationship access per row without eager-loading options.
PERF-PY-8.description: A SQLAlchemy relationship is accessed for every row in a processing loop while the query has no eager-loading option. This creates an N+1 query pattern; load the required relationships with joinedload or selectinload before processing the batch.
PERF-PY-8.detection_notes: Match a loop over query results/items followed by attribute access with relationship-like names (author, customer, profile, relation, parent, owner, account, organization) or an attribute used as an ORM object. Suppress an enclosing query with joinedload, selectinload, contains_eager, or explicit prefetching.

PERF-PY-9.name: JSON Payload Parse Then Re-Serialize
PERF-PY-9.original_description: Detect request JSON parsing followed by json.dumps before persistence.
PERF-PY-9.description: A request payload is parsed only to be serialized again before storage. The second conversion consumes CPU and can change byte representation; retain the validated raw body when byte-identical storage is appropriate.
PERF-PY-9.detection_notes: Match request.get_json(), request.json, json.loads(request.body/data), or await request.json() whose result reaches json.dumps or str before an ORM create/assignment in the same function. Suppress transformations that intentionally redact, normalize, or select a subset of the payload.

PERF-PY-10.name: Worker Sleeps After Successful Batch
PERF-PY-10.original_description: Detect an unconditional poll sleep after a non-empty worker run.
PERF-PY-10.description: A polling worker sleeps for its full interval even after it successfully processed work. Backlog latency is then inflated by the poll interval; continue immediately while batches are non-empty and sleep only when the queue is empty.
PERF-PY-10.detection_notes: Match a loop that assigns a run_once/process/claim result, conditionally logs or checks it, and then unconditionally calls time.sleep or await asyncio.sleep. Suppress an explicit continue/return before sleep on the successful-result branch, rate-limit sleeps, and cron-style one-shot commands.

PERF-PY-11.name: Per-Row ORM Mutation Instead Of Set-Based Update
PERF-PY-11.original_description: Detect all() followed by simple field mutation and a final commit.
PERF-PY-11.description: Rows are fully loaded, mutated one by one, and committed as a batch when the change is expressible as a set-based update. Hydration and per-row unit-of-work tracking add avoidable overhead; use QuerySet.update or SQLAlchemy update for uniform changes.
PERF-PY-11.detection_notes: Match query.all() or Model.objects.filter(...) iterated with a uniform assignment such as row.status = literal, followed by one session.commit() or save loop. Suppress when each row has distinct calculations, model hooks are required, or the row is used for an external side effect.

PERF-PY-12.name: Unbounded JSON Request Body Parse
PERF-PY-12.original_description: Detect JSON parsing from an HTTP request body without an apparent size cap.
PERF-PY-12.description: An endpoint parses the complete request body as JSON without an earlier size check. Large payloads consume memory and CPU on the request path; reject bodies above the service limit before decoding and preserve the framework's streaming semantics where available.
PERF-PY-12.detection_notes: Match json.loads(request.body/data), request.get_json(), request.json, or await request.json() in route/view functions without a preceding Content-Length/body-length comparison or configured parser limit in the same function. Suppress known framework-level request size limits and explicitly streamed parsers.

PERF-PY-13.name: Full ORM Hydration For Projection Read
PERF-PY-13.original_description: Detect model hydration when only a small set of fields is consumed.
PERF-PY-13.description: A read path hydrates full Django or SQLAlchemy model objects but uses only a small projection of their fields. This increases allocation, relationship bookkeeping, and transfer cost; use values, values_list, only, defer, or an explicit column selection where it preserves behavior.
PERF-PY-13.detection_notes: Match queryset iteration or .all() where each loop body reads one or two scalar fields from the model and does not call methods or access relationships. Suppress serializers, templates, ORM lifecycle hooks, and code already using values, values_list, only, defer, load_only, or explicit select columns.

PERF-PY-14.name: Select-Then-Insert Idempotency Check
PERF-PY-14.original_description: Detect a lookup for an idempotency key followed by a separate create operation.
PERF-PY-14.description: An idempotency path first queries for an existing key and then inserts in a separate operation. Concurrent requests pay an unnecessary read and can race into duplicate work; use a unique constraint with an atomic upsert, insert-on-conflict, or integrity-error recovery.
PERF-PY-14.detection_notes: Match a branch that calls get/filter/first for a variable named idempotency_key, request_id, event_id, or dedupe key and later calls create/add/insert for the same model. Suppress dialect-specific upserts, get_or_create with an enforced unique constraint, and code that handles integrity conflicts.
